title: Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QC Ultra in the US (2026) — which over-ear headphones should you buy
description: Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QuietComfort Ultra compared for US shoppers: live US$ prices, noise cancellation, sound signature, call quality and battery, plus a buying recommendation for commuters, office workers, frequent flyers and Android/iOS households.
heroTitle: Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QC Ultra in the US — 2026 live price comparison
heroTitleTemplate: Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QC Ultra in the US (2026) — from {floorPrice} for the XM6 today
heroBody: The Sony WH-1000XM6 and the Bose QuietComfort Ultra are the two flagship over-ear noise-cancelling headphones most US shoppers compare in 2026. Sony leads on outright noise cancellation depth, battery life and codec support, plus deeper EQ customisation through the Sony app. Bose keeps the edge on call quality, a more neutral default sound and a slightly more comfortable long-wearing shape on smaller heads. Pricing in the US is split between Amazon, Best Buy, Sony and Bose direct stores, and a long tail of marketplace resellers — the same pair can be hundreds of US$ apart between a renewed Bose listing and a Sony direct store, so a side-by-side is the only honest way to compare. This page pulls live US WH-1000XM6 and QC Ultra listings from BuyWhere's catalog so you can see the current US$ floor for each pair.

highlightSectionTitle: What actually separates the WH-1000XM6 from the QC Ultra

highlights.title: Noise cancellation leadership depends on what you're cancelling
highlights.body: Sony's WH-1000XM6 is class-leading on plane drone and HVAC hum. The QC Ultra is the better performer on office chatter and voices. If your daily noise is a mix of commuting and open-office work, the XM6 is the safer choice; if your priority is taming co-workers and call clarity, the QC Ultra pulls ahead.

highlights.title: Sound signature is the loudest personal preference
highlights.body: Sony ships a warm, bass-forward default that works well for pop, hip-hop and gaming. Bose ships a flatter, more neutral sound that critics and audiophiles tend to prefer out of the box. Both are easy to EQ in their respective apps, so if you have strong preferences either can be re-tuned.

highlights.title: Battery life is the quiet XM6 advantage
highlights.body: Sony's ~30 hours versus Bose's ~24 hours is a meaningful gap for long-haul flyers and work-trip users. USB-C fast-charge is faster on the XM6 too — a few minutes at the gate gets you through a transcontinental flight.

highlights.title: Call quality is the quiet QC Ultra advantage
highlights.body: Bose's beam-forming mic array is clearly better on windy calls, conference bridges and outdoor conversations. If you take calls on these headphones daily, the QC Ultra is the smarter buy even if its noise cancellation is slightly behind.

adviceSectionTitle: How to choose between WH-1000XM6 and QC Ultra in the US
advicePoints: Choose the Sony WH-1000XM6 if you commute on noisy transit, fly long-haul regularly, prioritise battery life, and use Android with LDAC support. The app's EQ and codec flexibility are also a plus for tinkerers.

Choose the Bose QC Ultra if you take a lot of calls, work in an open office, own other Bose products (Soundbar, QuietComfort Earbuds) and want SimpleSync pairing, or prefer a more neutral default sound.

Compare renewed Bose listings against new Sony pricing. A factory-renewed QuietComfort Ultra with a meaningful discount changes the value case significantly; check the seller and warranty terms before buying.

Try the fit before paying if possible. Both are light, but the XM6 clamps slightly firmer, which some glasses-wearers find tiring after a few hours. The QC Ultra's lower clamp is easier on smaller heads.

Watch for US holiday pricing on both. Sony and Bose both discount deeply during Prime Day, Black Friday and back-to-school. If you can wait, the gap between MSRP and the live floor price grows meaningfully during those windows.

Skip the most expensive refurbished listings. US shoppers who want warranty should buy new from Sony, Bose, Amazon, Best Buy, B&H or other major retailers; marketplace resellers can be cheaper but the warranty falls back to the shop.
faqSectionTitle: Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QC Ultra in the US — common questions

faqs.question: Which has better noise cancellation, Sony WH-1000XM6 or Bose QC Ultra?
faqs.answer: The Sony WH-1000XM6 leads on plane drone and HVAC hum. The Bose QC Ultra leads on office chatter and voices. For mixed commuting and open-office use the XM6 is usually the safer pick; for call-heavy work the QC Ultra pulls ahead.

faqs.question: Which is better for phone and video calls?
faqs.answer: The Bose QC Ultra is the better call headset, with clearer voice pickup on windy and outdoor calls. The Sony WH-1000XM6 is good in quiet rooms but loses more detail in noisy environments.

faqs.question: How long does the battery last on each?
faqs.answer: The Sony WH-1000XM6 lasts up to about 30 hours with ANC on, and fast-charges quickly over USB-C. The Bose QC Ultra lasts up to about 24 hours per charge.

faqs.question: Are both compatible with iPhone and Android?
faqs.answer: Yes for basic audio and calls. Android users gain LDAC support on the Sony WH-1000XM6 for higher-bitrate wireless audio; iPhone users stay on AAC on both. Multipoint pairing is supported on both for switching between two devices.

faqs.question: Should I buy a renewed Bose QC Ultra to save money?
faqs.answer: Often yes. Bose's certified renewed program carries a US warranty and typically sells at a meaningful discount to new. Marketplace renewals from third parties are cheaper still, but warranty falls back to the seller — read the listing carefully before paying.

categoryIntro.heading: Why US over-ear headphone prices vary so much
categoryIntro.body: In the United States the same pair of flagship headphones is sold by Sony and Bose directly, by major retailers like Amazon, Best Buy and B&H Photo, by carrier stores and by a long tail of marketplace and renewed resellers. Prices move with Prime Day, Black Friday and back-to-school rather than with the manufacturer, which is why a static 'best price' article goes stale within days and why this page reads live listings instead. Renewed and refurbished listings can cut the price by a third or more, but the warranty on those units falls back to the seller, not to Sony or Bose.
